concepts.heading: Understanding Neurodivergence
concepts.alt: A guide smiling with colourful gears and stars floating above his head
concepts.plain: Neurodivergence means natural differences in how brains work, like autism and ADHD.

concepts.heading: What Neurodivergence Is (and Isn't)
concepts.alt: Each holding a differently shaped puzzle piece that fits with the others
concepts.plain: These differences are part of human variety, not defects to fix.

concepts.heading: Neurodivergence in Relationships
concepts.alt: Two guides building a model together with great concentration
concepts.plain: Neurodivergent partners often bring loyalty, honesty and deep focus.

concepts.heading: Neurodivergence and the ENM/LGBTQ+ Overlap
concepts.plain: Many neurodivergent people are also LGBTQ+ or have more than one partner.

checks.prompt: The neurodiversity paradigm frames neurological differences as…
checks.explanation: Natural human variation. The neurodiversity paradigm — pioneered by autistic sociologist Judy Singer in the late 1990s — frames neurological differences as natural human variation rather than deficits to be cured.

checks.prompt: Which strength do neurodivergent people often bring to relationships?
options: Deep loyalty once trust is established
checks.explanation: Deep loyalty once trust is established. The lesson lists deep loyalty and commitment once trust is established, along with honest, direct communication.

37dac62b-c406-43ce-86f3-20f30e4805fa.takeaway: Brains work in different ways. Different is not broken.

concepts.heading: Sensory Needs & Physical Intimacy
concepts.alt: Wrapped in a soft blanket wearing big headphones, content
concepts.plain: How your senses take in touch, sound and light changes how closeness feels.

concepts.heading: How Sensory Processing Differs
concepts.alt: A guide adjusting a big volume dial
concepts.plain: Some people feel things too strongly. Others need more to feel anything.

concepts.heading: Impact on Physical Intimacy
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting side by side, D offering an open hand and A gently placing hers on it
concepts.plain: Light touch can bother some people, while firm pressure feels good. Ask.

concepts.heading: Communication Tools for Sensory Needs
concepts.alt: A guide holding up three round cards coloured green, yellow and red
concepts.plain: Use traffic lights: green means go on, yellow means slow down, red means stop.

concepts.heading: For Neurotypical Partners
concepts.alt: A guide listening patiently with a hand on his heart
concepts.plain: If your partner is neurodivergent, do not take sensory limits personally.

checks.explanation: Experiencing sensory input more intensely. Hypersensitivity is being over-responsive to touch, sound, light or other input.

checks.prompt: In the traffic light system, what does yellow mean?
options: I'm approaching my limit, slow down or check in
checks.explanation: I'm approaching my limit, slow down or check in. Green means this feels great, yellow means slow down or check in, and red means stop.

e3ef4ccf-1474-497e-b988-ce5179062dd5.takeaway: Sensory needs are real. Ask what feels good, and agree on simple signals.

concepts.heading: Communication Differences
concepts.alt: Talking, one with a square speech bubble and one with a round speech bubble
concepts.plain: Neurodivergent and neurotypical people often talk in different styles.

concepts.heading: The Double Empathy Problem
concepts.alt: Each building half of a small bridge toward the other across a gap
concepts.plain: Misreading happens in both directions. It is not one side lacking empathy.

concepts.heading: Common Communication Differences
concepts.alt: A guide holding a straight arrow while a curly arrow floats beside him
concepts.plain: Some people say things directly and mean exactly that. Others hint.

concepts.heading: Bridging Strategies
concepts.alt: Two guides shaking hands over a notepad with a checklist
concepts.plain: Agree out loud: we say what we mean, and we ask when unsure.

concepts.heading: In Polyamorous Contexts
concepts.plain: With more partners there are more styles to learn. Go one person at a time.

checks.prompt: The "double empathy problem" challenges which old assumption?
options: That everyone communicates the same way
checks.explanation: That autistic people lack empathy. Researcher Damian Milton's "double empathy problem" challenges the outdated assumption that autistic people lack empathy.
Directly and literally. They often say exactly what they mean, without hints.

6e8cc479-1c8b-46db-9877-f96a6d89358f.takeaway: Misunderstandings go both ways. Say what you mean and ask instead of guessing.

concepts.heading: Executive Function & Neurodivergent-Affirming Relationships
concepts.alt: A guide juggling a calendar, a clock and a to-do list, a little overwhelmed
concepts.plain: Executive function is the brain's planner. It often works differently in neurodivergent people.

concepts.heading: What Executive Function Affects
concepts.alt: A guide looking at a clock and a pile of unsorted papers
concepts.plain: It affects starting tasks, keeping time, remembering and switching between things.

concepts.heading: The "Lazy" Myth
concepts.alt: A guide straining to push a huge boulder uphill, determined
concepts.plain: It is not laziness. The brain spends its energy differently.

concepts.heading: Practical Strategies for Couples
concepts.alt: Happily swapping chores, C handing D a broom while holding a calculator
concepts.plain: Split tasks by who finds them easy, not by a strict half-and-half.

concepts.heading: The Parent-Child Dynamic Trap
concepts.plain: If one partner manages everything, it starts to feel like parent and child. Avoid that.

concepts.heading: Principles of Neurodivergent-Affirming Love
concepts.alt: Two guides forming a heart shape together with their hands
concepts.plain: Accept your partner's brain as it is, and work with it.

concepts.heading: Building an Affirming Home
concepts.alt: A guide arranging a cosy corner with a lamp, cushions and a wall calendar
concepts.plain: Set up your home to help, with quiet corners, soft light and clear routines.

concepts.heading: When Both Partners Are Neurodivergent
concepts.plain: Two neurodivergent partners can understand each other deeply and still need systems.

concepts.heading: Resources for Neurodivergent Couples
concepts.plain: There are books and research made for neurodivergent couples.

checks.prompt: What does the lesson say about the "lazy" label?
options: It is true for most people
checks.explanation: Neurodivergent people aren't lazy. Neurodivergent people aren't lazy — they have a brain that allocates resources differently.

checks.prompt: What can happen when one partner takes over all the planning tasks?
options: The relationship can slip into a parent-child dynamic
checks.explanation: The relationship can slip into a parent-child dynamic. When one partner takes over all executive function tasks, the relationship can slip into a parent-child dynamic.

c2541d6d-e409-402b-82cc-e681736fd625.takeaway: Trouble with planning is not laziness. Split tasks to fit each brain and build routines that help.
